answer: Single active job chaining stops alias farming. Each alias holds one paid job at a time, and the next job unlocks only after the client signs the reef survey receipt and a 3 epoch gap passes. An alias that starts a second job early triggers a freeze, and a checker compares timestamps on its ivory inventory log and its nadir depth reading. A confirmed overlap loses that epoch pay and bars the alias for 20 epochs, while the client who reports it earns a 15 percent bonus on the next job. One operator cannot run many aliases when every alias moves one job at a time.
